newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus jails Israeli for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus jails Israeli for fraud.

text.p: An Israeli telephone salesman was jailed for two-and-a-half years in Cyprus on Wednesday after pleading guilty to possessing forged dollar bills.
Avi Biton, 21, from Haifa, pleaded guilty to possessing 72 forged 100-dollar bills when he was arrested in the southern coastal resort of Larnaca on August 30.

Next week he, his alleged accomplice and another two Israelis are due before the same criminal court in capital Nicosia in connection with their daring, but bungled bid to escape from custody as they were being taken to court on September 11.
Biton's Cypriot lawyer told the Criminal Court, which convened in Larnaca, that the accused, formerly a member of Israel's under-21 soccer team, did not know the bills were counterfeit.
Biton was caught when he attempted to exchange one of the bills at a local bank. When police were called in they discovered another 71 bills concealed in a sock.
He was jailed for a year for attempting to circulate the notes and another 2.5 years for possession. The two sentences are to run concurrently, the three-bench court ruled.
Biton's alleged accomplice, Shuki Samana, 24, also from Haifa, pleaded not guilty to the charges. He is due to stand trial on November 11.
The two accused are due to appear before the same criminal court, due to sit in Nicosia on October 30. They face charges of attempting to escape arrest.

The two men who allegedly helped them, Biton's brother David, 24, and Amor Shimon, 28, are charged with assisting their escape, possession of firearms, conspiring to commit a crime and causing damage to a police vehicle.
Police allege David Biton and Shimon waylaid a police car in central Nicosia taking the other two to court in Larnaca.

Brandishing a pistol -- which police now suspect was a toy -- David Biton and Shimon got the other two suspects out of the police vehicle, put them on the back of their high-powered motorcycles and charged through a United Nations checkpoint close by leading to Turkish-held northern Cyprus.
Their freedom was short-lived. Turkish Cypriot police returned them the same day.
